rationale: Repairs an internal contradiction between two limitation entries about the boundary case's batch-size coverage, introduced when the extended boundary receipt was cited.

interpretations.rationale: Consistency note: this successor merges two limitation entries that described the same boundary result differently - the older wording still said the boundary case used one batch size after the extended harness had measured it at two - so the account no longer contains contradictory statements about that setting; sources, executions, knowledge uses, conclusion and counterevidence are unchanged. Extension note: this successor cites the extended boundary harness (receipt f394d8354fab48138079db19ca3deb13), which measures the boundary at the library's default batch size as well as at 16, so the account's central quantitative claim rests on two batch sizes; sources, the other executions, knowledge uses, conclusion and counterevidence are otherwise unchanged. Extension note: this successor cites the revised availability harness (receipt 7ac7e4f67d194ad5b4e196c9b73f9897), which adds a case at the default batch size and reproduces the consequence there, so the account's availability claim no longer rests on a single batch size; the other executions, sources, knowledge uses, conclusion and counterevidence are unchanged. Correction note: the behaviour this account relied on for the default snapshot cadence has been refined. The earlier statement described the automatic cadence as keeping the committed range above the snapshot near SnapshotThreshold; the default-configuration receipt shows a node whose committed range stood 12001 entries above an absent snapshot while the threshold was 8192 and no snapshot had been taken (receipt 0cb30b6bf8874d479b83653bd4e6c553, event 36), which is a margin of roughly one and a half times the threshold rather than a value near it. The cause is that runSnapshots evaluates shouldSnapshot only when a randomized timeout of up to SnapshotInterval expires (snapshot.go:71-95), so between checks the range can pass the threshold and keep growing. Knowledge revision 2 states this; the counterevidence about the burst workload and the statement that how long a node typically stays above the bound is unmeasured both still hold. Extension note: this successor cites the repeat of the bound experiment (receipt 962196ed81fd46cfb9476bbd63c2c637), which reproduced the below-bound and above-bound cases with identical operands, so every pair in this account now has at least two executions; sources, the other executions, knowledge uses, conclusion and counterevidence are otherwise unchanged. Extension note: this successor records that the availability pair has been executed three times, not once - the two later receipts were produced by the other investigation's multi-node harness, which contains this pair among its four cases - and corrects the schedule-variation limitation accordingly; sources, the other executions, knowledge uses, conclusion and counterevidence are unchanged. Extension note: this successor adds the second execution of the fixed experiment (receipt 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2) as reproducibility evidence for the boundary and default-configuration pairs; sources, knowledge uses, conclusion and the other executions are unchanged, and the counterevidence and limitation that described those pairs as single-run are updated accordingly. Precision note: the entry-based batch figures recorded by the earlier receipts equal the delivered counts there, and the receipts' own operands show why. In receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f event 16 the prefix ends at log index 9002 with staged commit index 9001, so the replayed range holds the bootstrap configuration entry, one no-op and 8999 commands, that is 9000 tuples, and ceil(9000/64) = 141, the figure the receipt records for that case. Receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 records 1501 and 3001 replayed entries with 94 and 188 batches at MaxAppendEntries 16, and the same counting gives 1500 and 3000 tuples, ceil(1500/16) = 94 and ceil(3000/16) = 188. The two counts diverge only where the replayed range ends inside a batch in a way that adds a no-op, which is what the boundary receipt's 2049-entry range with 128 delivered batches shows. Reproducibility: the fixed experiment that produced the boundary and default-configuration pairs was executed a second time from its retained inputs in a clean copy (receipt 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2), and every decisive operand came back identical - the 2049-entry range again held 2048 tuples in 128 batches and returned in 0ms (events 30, 31, 32), the 2050-entry range again held 2049 tuples in 129 batches and did not return with three stack samples (events 33, 34, 35), and the default-configuration prefix again recorded staged commit index 12001 with snapshot index 0 and no snapshots listed against a bound of 8192, with the replay-enabled restart not returning and the control returning (events 36 to 41). The only differing operand was the control's return latency, 3ms in the first execution and 1ms in the repeat. A citation check of this account against the retained observations found no other discrepancy. Correction note: this successor extends the previous account of this question with the default-configuration receipt; sources, the earlier executions, knowledge uses, conclusions and limitations are otherwise unchanged, and the counterevidence item that recorded default-cadence reachability as unmeasured is replaced by the measured statement. Correction note: this successor differs from the previous account of this question only in two transcribed numbers and their attribution; the flag-off control of receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f returned in 1ms and the same control of receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 returned in 5ms, as those receipts record, and the earlier account had them swapped. Everything else - sources, executions, knowledge uses, counterevidence, limitations and joint history - is unchanged. Mechanism. With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs set, NewRaft reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs with it before starting any background goroutine (api.go:723-754). processLogs walks the committed range and appends a commit tuple only for entries prepareLog accepts - commands and barriers always, configuration entries when protocolVersion > 2, and nothing for no-op or deprecated peer entries - flushing a batch whenever the batch reaches config.MaxAppendEntries and delivering it through a select whose only other case is shutdownCh (raft.go:1296-1364 with prepareLog at raft.go:1364-1391). fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 (api.go:560) and its only consumer runFSM is started by api.go:636-638 after the replay returns, so a replay needing more than 128 delivered batches waits for a consumer that cannot exist until the blocked call finishes, with no timeout. Block and bound. Receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f restarts a single-voter prefix holding 9001 committed entries above an absent snapshot (event 16, 141 delivered batches at MaxAppendEntries 64); the flag-on restart admitted by event 17 did not return within 8000ms (event 18, stack naming processLogs at raft.go:1346 called from restoreFromCommittedLogs at api.go:753 called from NewRaft) while the flag-off restart of the same shape returned in 1ms (event 21) and became leader (event 22); receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 reproduces both, with its own flag-off control returning in 5ms (its event 21) and adds a pair at MaxAppendEntries 16 where 1501 replayed entries (94 batches) returned in 0ms (event 25) and 3001 entries (188 batches) did not (event 29). Receipt 8a710c75d1814aafad5d24b536998539 then places the boundary exactly: at MaxAppendEntries 16 one prefix ends at staged commit index 2049, whose replayed range contains 2048 entries that become commit tuples, that is 128 delivered batches (event 31), and NewRaft returned in 0ms (event 32, comparison holds); the other ends at 2050 with 2049 tuples, that is 129 delivered batches (event 34), and NewRaft did not return within 8000ms (event 35, comparison violated, three stack mentions naming the replay frames). The pair differs only in one replayed command, so the bound is the 128-slot channel measured in delivered batches, and any count derived from the log's index range is an upper bound: the entry-based figure for the returning case also reads 129 batches (event 31), because the range includes entries that produce no tuple. Default configuration. Receipt 0cb30b6bf8874d479b83653bd4e6c553 builds two further single-voter prefixes with Config.DefaultConfig values left untouched: event 36 records SnapshotThreshold 8192, MaxAppendEntries 64, SnapshotInterval 120s, 12000 applied commands, staged commit index 12001, snapshot index 0, no snapshots listed, and a committed range of 12001 entries above the snapshot against the bound of 128*64 = 8192 tuples; the flag-on restart did not return within 8000ms with four stack samples naming the replay frames (event 38, comparison violated), while the flag-off control returned in 3ms (event 41, comparison holds). The trigger therefore needs no tuning of threshold or batch size: the automatic snapshot loop wakes on a randomized timeout of up to SnapshotInterval (snapshot.go:71-95), so a node that commits faster than that cadence carries a range above the bound into its restart. Availability. Receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a builds three voters at MaxAppendEntries 16, commits 3000 commands through a leader that is not A (event 9), restarts A in a goroutine, and observes the same non-return (event 10). With the replay on the group kept committing with two members live and lost the ability after one further member was stopped (event 11: commit_while_two_live_ok true, commit_after_stop_ok false, error 'leadership lost while committing log'), while with the replay off the same stop left the pair {leader, A} live and the command succeeded (events 13, 14). That pair reproduced identically in two later executions of the same harness (receipts fe822d82c6264158826e0303b4ce59b1 and 67fc59b525e54d01b709a19592689357, events 9 to 14 in each: staged commit index 3001 with the replay enabled and 3000 with it disabled, the replay-enabled restart not returning, the group committing with two members live and losing the ability after the second stop, and the control returning in 0ms and committing), so the availability consequence now rests on three executions with the same split, and a fourth at the library's default batch size: receipt 7ac7e4f67d194ad5b4e196c9b73f9897 records a prefix with 9000 committed commands and MaxAppendEntries 64 (event 15: staged commit index 9001, 141 batches by the entry-based count, snapshot index 0), the replay-enabled restart not returning with two stack samples naming the replay frames (event 16), the group committing while two members were live and losing that ability after the second stop (event 17, comparison violated). The consequence therefore does not depend on the smaller batch size used in the earlier cases. The corrected unit matters for the recorded gaps: the three correction gaps ask about the premise change, and the receipt answers them substantively - the returning case's entry-based figure was 129 batches while only 128 were delivered, so counts derived from a log index range are upper bounds. Defect account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft cannot complete startup whenever the replay delivers more than 128 batches, that is more than 128*MaxAppendEntries entries that become commit tuples above the restored snapshot index; at the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 that is 8192 tuples, and it is proportionally smaller for any smaller legal value, as measured at 16 (2048 tuples returning, 2049 blocking). The failure is a startup liveness failure: the node never begins participating, so a single-voter group stays down, a larger group runs with proportionally less fault tolerance, and one further stop was enough to make a three-voter group unable to commit. Pending operations the leader had accepted are answered with ErrLeadershipLost once it steps down (raft.go:508-528). Reproducibility of the bound pair: receipt 962196ed81fd46cfb9476bbd63c2c637 is a second execution of the same fixed experiment and returns the same operands as receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 - events 23 and 25 record 1501 replayed entries with 94 batches and a return in 0ms, events 27 and 29 record 3001 entries with 188 batches and no return with the replay frames in the stack, and the only differing operand is the flag-off control's return latency, 5ms then 3ms. Boundary at a second batch size: the same harness now places the replay on both sides of the channel's capacity at the default MaxAppendEntries of 64. Receipt f394d8354fab48138079db19ca3deb13 records 8193 staged entries holding 8192 tuples in 128 delivered batches that returned in 2ms (events 36 to 38), and 8194 staged entries holding 8193 tuples in 129 delivered batches that did not return, with four stack samples naming the replay frames (events 39 to 41). With the 16-batch pair that puts the boundary at 128 delivered batches at two batch sizes, that is 128 * MaxAppendEntries tuples, 2048 and 8192 respectively, rather than a property of one setting.

knowledge.assertion: Batches are counted in commit tuples, so no-op and deprecated peer entries consume no batch slot and configuration entries do so only above protocol version 2.
fsmMutateCh has capacity 128 and its consumer runFSM starts only after the startup replay returns.

The snapshot check is only evaluated when a randomized timeout of up to SnapshotInterval expires, so the committed range above the newest snapshot can exceed SnapshotThreshold by a wide margin between checks.
With the flag on, lastApplied is set to the persisted commit index before the replay, so the replay range spans the committed log above the snapshot.
The tracked latest configuration feeds quorumSize and the vote-admission checks, which is why a member that never starts is simply absent from every future majority.

counterevidence: The block itself is evidenced by non-return within an 8000ms window plus a stack sample per blocked case (events 18, 29, 10 and 35). The permanence argument does not rest on those samples: the source shows no timeout, a single consumer started only after the blocked call returns, and an escape requiring an object the caller has not received. The flag-off controls return promptly in each receipt: 1ms at event 21 of receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f, 5ms at event 21 and 0ms at event 25 of receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00, and 0ms at event 13 of receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a.

The boundary pair has now been executed twice from the same fixed inputs in separate clean copies with identical operands (receipts 8a710c75d1814aafad5d24b536998539 and 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2), but its delivered-tuple count is computed by the harness scanning the replayed range with the same type rule prepareLog uses rather than read from an internal counter; the behaviour straddles the boundary by one replayed command, and the tuple figure is an inspectable operand rather than the decisive predicate.

The default-configuration case is a burst: the harness applies commands as fast as the in-memory stack allows and no automatic snapshot had fired at restart (event 36: snapshot index 0, no snapshots listed). It reproduced identically in the second execution of the same fixed experiment (receipt 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2, events 36 to 41). It shows that default settings do not keep the range below the bound during a burst, not how long a node typically stays above it, and the other cases that raised SnapshotThreshold made the condition permanent rather than momentary.

The availability case contains a deliberate second stop, so what it shows is the loss of the group's fault-tolerance margin rather than an outage in an untouched cluster; the control with the replay disabled performs the same stop and still commits, which is what attributes the loss to the member that did not return.

In the flag-on availability case the surviving leader's command failed with 'leadership lost while committing log', which is the leader stepping down and failing its pending operations rather than a defect of its own; the same apply succeeded while two members were live (event 11) and after the same stop in the control (event 14).

The blocked NewRaft call is abandoned in a separate goroutine so the tests can complete; that is a harness choice, not a repair, and no harness observes the process-level consequence of a caller that waits forever.

The boundary is measured with harness-derived tuple counts at both batch sizes (receipts 8a710c75d1814aafad5d24b536998539 and f394d8354fab48138079db19ca3deb13): the count comes from scanning the replayed range with the same type rule prepareLog applies, not from an internal counter, and each side has been executed once at the larger batch size and twice at the smaller one.
limitations: All cases run in one process over in-memory transports and a test commit-tracking store; no production store, no process-level restart and no disk fault are exercised, and the confined goroutine is the only trace of the real caller's hang.

The availability case uses one prefix shape and one extra stop, with two batch sizes now exercised (16 and the default 64); the boundary case now spans two batch sizes (16 and the default 64) with one run per side at the larger one, so the single-setting results are the 9000-entry pair, the bound pair and the default-configuration pair as to batch size; observation windows are 8000ms for restarts and 3000ms for the applies.

Schedule variation is unevenly covered: the original 9000-entry pair appears in two receipts, the boundary pair and the default-configuration pair have each been executed twice from the same fixed inputs with identical operands, the bound pair has now been executed twice with identical operands, and the availability pair three times with the same split; each blocked state is still sampled once per execution.
The bound's dependence on the caller-side store is assumed rather than verified: the replay range comes from the stored commit index, whose durability contract belongs to the LogStore implementation.
interpretations.joint_history: All four receipts are executions of fixed experiments for this investigation on the same captured source revision, in separate workspaces with no shared mutable state, and their harnesses share the same initialization: an in-memory commit-tracking log store, a single-voter bootstrap for the first three, RestoreCommittedLogs enabled on the prefix, and the restart in a separate goroutine with an 8000ms window. Receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f and its revision e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 use one harness whose cases differ only in Config.MaxAppendEntries and the committed range, and e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 re-runs the original 9000-entry pair unchanged. Receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a uses a three-voter harness at the same MaxAppendEntries 16 and observes the same block. Receipt 8a710c75d1814aafad5d24b536998539 uses the first harness's prefix construction with targets chosen from an earlier construction run of the same case and places the replay on both sides of the channel capacity. The blocked state in every receipt is corroborated by a stack sample naming the replay frames, and no receipt depends on another's runtime state. Receipt 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2 is not a separate producer at all: it is the same fixed experiment as receipt 0cb30b6bf8874d479b83653bd4e6c553 executed a second time in a fresh clean copy, which is why its events carry the same names and indices. Receipt 0cb30b6bf8874d479b83653bd4e6c553 uses the same single-voter prefix construction with Config.DefaultConfig left in place for the snapshot settings, so its operands (staged commit index, snapshot index, replay batches) are directly comparable with the earlier receipts' fields of the same names. Two further receipts are shared with the configuration-recovery investigation: fe822d82c6264158826e0303b4ce59b1 and 67fc59b525e54d01b709a19592689357 are executions of that investigation's multi-node harness, which contains the availability case alongside its own cases, so their events 9 to 14 are the same case this investigation's receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a recorded, re-observed under the same fixed inputs. Receipt 962196ed81fd46cfb9476bbd63c2c637 is the same fixed experiment as receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 executed a second time in a fresh clean copy, which is why their events carry the same names and indices and only the flag-off return latencies differ (5ms and 3ms). Receipt 7ac7e4f67d194ad5b4e196c9b73f9897 is a revision of the availability experiment (16c25787045d480683724439289a6ecc-experiment revised as 0cad9d5f0a074906abf964f9d006b756-experiment), whose harness adds the default-batch case to the same file, so it re-observes the two earlier availability cases as well and, in the same file, the authority and vote cases that the configuration-recovery investigation relies on. Receipt f394d8354fab48138079db19ca3deb13 is a revision of the boundary experiment (3bdf46ca8b274b719cc26e672b951e75-experiment revised as a4d21936f18b47a082bcd77d54bb1b33-experiment) whose harness adds the default-batch pair to the same file, so it re-observes the 16-batch pair as well; the two runs agree on both sides of the boundary.
